headline: Chips Lead a Broad Friday Rally as Energy Risks Simmer Beneath the Surface
body_html:
Equities closed Friday's session on a firmly constructive note, with 396 of 545 names in our universe finishing higher — a breadth reading that signals genuine participation rather than a narrow index-driven lift. Semiconductors were the session's undisputed engine, advancing 3.15% as a cluster of power and connectivity names surged in sympathy with surging demand signals across the AI infrastructure chain. Homebuilders added 1.58% and Industrials gained 1.24%, underscoring a rotation toward rate-sensitive and cyclical corners of the market. Healthcare was the lone sector to close in the red, shedding a nominal fraction.

The standout mover of the day was Vicor Corporation, whose shares rocketed 11.15% to lead the entire universe. The power-module specialist was joined by ON Semiconductor and Synaptics — up 8.51% and 8.09%, respectively — in a sweep that confirmed semiconductors as Friday's clearest expression of risk appetite. NetApp surged 8.54% and CDW Corp climbed 7.85%, broadening the technology rally into storage hardware and IT distribution. On the other side of the ledger, Qualys shed nearly 7% and Kadant fell 6.96%, while metallurgical coal names Alpha Metallurgical Resources and Warrior Met Coal each dropped 3.82%.

Beneath the equity optimism, a geopolitical undercurrent warrants attention heading into the weekend. Houthi forces reaching a strategically significant Gulf island and drone strikes attributed to Iraq-based actors disrupting Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline rattled crude supply assumptions, even as Riyadh held its military response. Energy sector gains were muted at just 0.26% — a telling gap relative to broader market strength — suggesting traders are pricing in disruption risk without yet making a full directional bet on oil. The week closes on a constructive tape, but the Gulf situation is one worth watching as new information develops.

briefs.headline: Vicor Surges Past the Field in Power-Module Surge
briefs.body: Vicor Corporation finished Friday as the session's top performer, climbing 11.15% in heavy volume. The power-module maker benefited from accelerating interest in high-density power delivery solutions tied to data center build-outs. The move pulled several adjacent semiconductor and power names sharply higher alongside it.

briefs.headline: Gulf Pipeline Strike Clouds Crude Supply Outlook
briefs.body: Saudi Arabia confirmed that drones launched from Iraqi territory struck its East-West pipeline, forcing a shutdown and raising fresh concerns about Gulf energy infrastructure. Riyadh signaled it would not retaliate immediately, but the incident adds a new layer of uncertainty to already fragile crude supply buffers, according to Chevron's chief executive.

briefs.headline: 25 Years On: Markets Open Solemnly as the Nation Reflects
briefs.body: Friday's session opened against the backdrop of nationwide commemorations marking the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks. Ceremonies across the country paused to honor the nearly 3,000 lives lost, a moment that colored pre-market sentiment before equities found their footing and rallied decisively through the afternoon.

briefs.headline: QatarEnergy Moves to Lock In U.S. LNG Supply Through 2031
briefs.body: QatarEnergy is actively pursuing long-term liquefied natural gas agreements with American exporters stretching as far as 2031, according to people familiar with the discussions. The push reflects Doha's strategy to diversify its supply relationships and secure volumes ahead of anticipated tightness in global LNG markets later this decade.

briefs.headline: Anthropic Discloses Misuse Cases for Its Claude AI System
briefs.body: Artificial intelligence firm Anthropic detailed instances in which its Claude model was exploited for purposes including weapons research, espionage, and cyber operations. The disclosure highlights the mounting compliance and reputational challenges facing AI developers as regulators and the public demand greater accountability over model deployment.

briefs.headline: Election Officials Move to Restrict Prediction-Market Trading
briefs.body: Regulators overseeing U.S. elections announced a prohibition on certain categories of public-sector workers trading on political prediction markets ahead of November's midterm elections. Officials cited concerns about conflicts of interest and the potential for insider advantage, adding a new wrinkle to the fast-growing and still loosely regulated prediction-market industry.
